title: Quantum security of Bourgain's two-source extractor against qma
summary: Determine whether Bourgain's explicit two-source extractor remains secure against the quantum measurement adversary throughout its classical entropy regime.

formal_statement.body: Let $\operatorname{Ext}_{\mathrm{B}}$ be Bourgain's explicit two-source extractor cited by the source, with two $n$-bit sources of min-entropy at least $(1/2-\delta)n$ for an admissible constant $\delta>0$. Prove the source's Definition 5 trace-distance extraction guarantee for $\operatorname{Ext}_{\mathrm{B}}$ against every admissible $\ell$-qma state, with explicit output length and error throughout the classical parameter regime, or exhibit a valid qma state that violates the guarantee.

scope.domain: Bourgain's explicit two-source extractor under quantum measurement adversary side information
assumptions: The two source registers and adversarial side information form an admissible l-qma state in the source's Definition 3
Each n-bit source has min-entropy at least (1/2-delta)n for a constant delta supported by Bourgain's construction
Security uses the source's trace-distance extractor definition
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later theorem proves qma security for Bourgain's exact construction over this complete entropy and adversary regime; quantum-secure results for inner product or different extractor constructions do not settle it.

citations.label: Aggarwal--Boddu--Jain--Obremski, Quantum Measurement Adversary
citations.locator: Section VI-C, Open Questions 1 and 3, journal p. 334

progress.summary: The source asks whether Bourgain's two-source extractor is secure against qma at its classical min-entropy threshold.
